content.title: A Stock Market Priced for Perfection Can Still Have a Very Good Year
content.summary: Christmas week sparked a Santa Claus rally, but a stock market that’s posted three straight years of above-average gains will have to wrestle with a simple fact of life—it’s incredibly hard to stay perfect.  The S&P 500 is expected to grow earnings by 15% in 2026, per FactSet, while net profit margins are forecast to hit 13.9%, the highest since FactSet began tracking the metric in 2008.  Meanwhile, economic growth forecasts are moving higher after a stellar third-quarter gross-domestic-product reading, inflation isn’t expected to be a problem, and the labor market should be able to hold on.

content.title: Jobless Claims Fall. What That Means for Fed Rate Cuts.
content.summary: The number of Americans filing for initial unemployment benefits dropped last week, suggesting the labor market is still in a relatively good place as the year draws to a close.  The jobless claims number fell by 10,000 to 214,00 for the week ended Dec. 20, according to Labor Department data published on Wednesday.  The drop in jobless claims is good news for the economy, although a stronger labor market may weaken the case for the Federal Reserve to carry on cutting interest rates in early 2026, which would be disappointing for the market.
